## What changed from the original calendar

The first version of this page ran fifteen consecutive Thursdays, 9/3 to 12/10. Three things moved it:

- **Chuseok.** 9/24 falls in the 추석 연휴, so there is no class that week. Rather than lose a session, every session from the old Week 4 onward runs **one week later**, and the final defense moves into Week 16 (12/17), the university's official make-up week. If you saw "Week 4 — Theoretical point of departure" on an earlier version, that session is now **Week 5 on 10/1**.
- **Conference Thursdays.** In two weeks the Thursday slot is unavailable, so the session meets on the **Tuesday of the same week** instead: 11/3 and 11/24. Nothing else about those sessions changes — same format, same roles. The 10/22 conference is covered by the Tuesday 10/27 session described below.
- **A guest lecture, and one week built from two.** Dr. Kunhee Choi gives a special lecture on 10/29, so the pre-proposal presentations move to Week 10 (11/3) and everything after them shifts with it. To make that fit before the defense on 12/17, the survey-measurement week and the quantitative-modeling week are now a single session — Week 8, Tuesday 10/27 at 18:00. They were always one pipeline: you build an instrument, then you model what it produces. Weeks 11 to 16 keep both their numbers and their dates.

For sessions that are not on a Thursday, anything due "before class" is counted back from the day the class actually meets. Time and room for those sessions are announced on ETL.

No other session date in this span coincides with a 2026 Korean public holiday (Gaecheonjeol falls on Saturday 10/3, its substitute holiday on Monday 10/5; Hangeul Day falls on Friday 10/9).
